what_worked: All requested catalog navigation and hyperparameter reading completed through ordinary HTML links and HTTP GETs without repository knowledge, API, login or JavaScript.
The start guide directly exposed the requested title, avoiding any guessed hashed paper identifier.
The contents link identified the relevant bounded text part without opening all five parts or downloading the full graph.
All three Cited by pages opened; 24 + 24 + 19 entries matched the displayed count of 67 internal citation edges.
A citing paper reached from the last citation page exposed its own title, identifier, citation links and text links.
limits_and_friction: Strict use of the supplied web-open/search tools did not complete this journey; success required a direct HTTP retrieval fallback. This is not evidence that arbitrary browsing tools or other LLMs can consume the site.
Only this particular title journey was tested. DeepSeekMath appears as a start-page example, so general catalog title discovery was not measured.
The 67 edges are catalog-local; coverage of citations elsewhere on the web was not tested.
Section contents links share the coarse #text anchor within each part, so the exact section still must be found inside that part.
Math extraction includes duplicated rendered/LaTeX material and duplicated numerals, although the requested values were unambiguous.
No semantic search, REST/MCP service operation, deployment, original-source freshness, or cross-model compatibility was tested.
